log_1971.title: Station log, Sunday 14 November 1971
log_1971.text: 14.11.71 Sun. 16.22 SW 6, overcast, rain. Light exhibited. Lamp normal. / 16.40 Engine started. Batteries on charge, 41%. / 18.30 Radio check Stornoway CG. Gale warning, severe gale 9. / 18.50 Kittiwake (SY 37) brought in by North Sound on radio bearings. / 23.25 Stornoway CG on Ch. 16. All well.  (Hand: C. Mackay)

log_1953.title: Station log, 14-15 November 1953
log_1953.text: 14.11 23.30: I. Mackay on watch. Light good. / 15.11 01.30: Trawler observed standing in too close to East Gut. No response to light. / 02.10: Light extinguished approx. 2 min (mantle failure). Relit 02.12. / 02.30: Wreckage reported East Gut by Stornoway W/T. Mary Ellen (SY 214) believed lost. / Signed I. Mackay, P.K.  (The entries are in the same small square hand as tonight's log.)

letter_1957.title: Unsent letter, Christmas 1957
letter_1957.text:
Christmas 1957

Callum,

I made you write it. I made a boy of twenty-three put his hand to my lie, because I was asleep in this chair with the bottle, and the clockwork stuck on the bad tooth, and the light was out, and I could not face it.

The girl at Stornoway had it right. Ten minutes to two. I heard the wireless in my sleep and thought I was dreaming.

Ross was a better man than me, and he was my friend. If you ever have the courage I did not, put it right.

Your father,
Iain Mackay

note_046.title: Maintenance note, light console
note_046.text: GEAR RACE - worn tooth at 046°. Sticks in heavy weather. FREE BY HAND: take the drive off, back her past the tooth, then put the drive in again. Reported to Board 4.3.49. I.M. / Reported again 9.12.53. C.M. / Reported again 2.2.61. Engineer says "next refit". C.M.

inquiry_extract.title: Report of Formal Investigation, Mary Ellen (SY 214): extract
inquiry_extract.text: 22. The Court has considered a wireless message logged by Stornoway Coastguard at 01.52, which was said to report that no light was visible from North Point. The message was received in conditions of severe interference. The Court finds it confused and unreliable. 23. The Court prefers the evidence of the station log of North Point Light, kept by a principal keeper of long and unblemished service, which records that the light was exhibited throughout save for approximately two minutes at 02.10. 24. The Court finds that the master, Alasdair Ross, failed to keep a proper lookout and stood into danger despite the light being exhibited. APPENDIX C. Photostat of the station log, North Point Light, 14-15 November 1953. (The page shown is in a small square hand.)

clipping_1954.title: Stornoway Gazette, 18 March 1954
clipping_1954.text: MARY ELLEN INQUIRY: MASTER TO BLAME. ... the master, Alasdair Ross of Leverburgh, who is presumed drowned, "failed to keep a proper lookout and stood into danger despite the light being exhibited." Evidence from the station log of North Point Light ... showed that the light was extinguished for approximately two minutes only, at 2.10 a.m. ... A wireless message received at Stornoway shortly before the stranding was described by the court as "confused and unreliable." The sole survivor of the crew, deckhand Kenneth Bain, was below at the time ...

forecast.title: Teleprinter, 1600 GMT
forecast.text: GALE WARNING ISSUED 1600 GMT 14 NOV 1971. HEBRIDES MINCHES SOUTHWESTERLY SEVERE GALE 9 INCREASING STORM 10 IMMINENT.

photo_keepers.text: Iain & Callum Mackay, North Point, May 1952.

coat_note.title: Note in the oilskin pocket
coat_note.text:
Stores for the relief boat,
Thurs. if the sea allows

- paraffin for the stove (2 drums)
- No. 8 cells for the torch, a dozen
- tea, condensed milk, Skerry Flake
- glass for the west window, 2nd pane
   (cracked in the Sept. gale)

Tell Stornoway the No. 2 set still
smokes on starting.

C.M.

photo_1953.title: Photograph: the Mary Ellen's crew, July 1953
photo_1953.text: Eight men on a deck at Leverburgh pier. The one at the wheel is laughing. On the back, in pencil: "Mary Ellen, July 1953. A. Ross, master." Beneath, in another hand: "Kenny B. on the hatch."
